name: SSC CPO
fullName: Staff Selection Commission – Sub-Inspector in Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces Examination
approxCandidates: Several lakh applicants per cycle (official 2026 figure not published at check time)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree; 20–25 years (with category relaxations); Delhi Police SI (Exe.) male candidates need an LMV driving licence; physical standards and PET apply

notification.summary: SSC CPO 2026 was notified on 10 Sep 2026 for ≈1,871 tentative SI posts in Delhi Police, CAPFs and CISF (some reports say 2,018), with a revised Paper 1 pattern (100 questions, 1 hour). Applications closed on 30 Sep 2026, the correction window runs 8–10 Oct 2026, and Paper 1 is reportedly proposed for 20–28 Nov 2026.

pattern.notes: Revised in the 2026 notification (as reported by multiple coaching sites): Paper 1 cut from 200 questions/200 marks/2 hours to 100 questions/100 marks/1 hour, with a 15-minute timer per section; −0.25 per wrong answer. Paper 2 (English) reportedly expanded. Selection: Paper 1 → PET/PST → Paper 2 → DME. Verify on ssc.gov.in.

trendAnalysis.summary: Analysis is based on the 2023–2025 papers (old 50-questions-per-section format); the topic mix is expected to carry over to the shorter 2026 format. Paper 1 is moderate, close to CGL Tier 1 in level: Quant is the toughest (algebra, geometry, trigonometry, mensuration and DI ≈ 45% of the section), Reasoning is scoring (analogy, classification, series, coding, puzzles and figures), GK is static-heavy with a noticeable share of polity, history and police/defence-related questions, and English has vocabulary, grammar-based error spotting/improvement, narration and voice, plus cloze and comprehension. Sectional timing from 2026 makes time management per section critical.

resources.notes: SSC publishes tentative answer keys with candidates' response sheets (question papers) on ssc.gov.in for a short window after Paper 1 and Paper 2; final keys after results. No permanent official PYQ archive; memory-based papers are compiled by coaching sites.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first.
Pen : Write :: Knife : ?
questions.explanation: A pen is used to write; a knife is used to cut.

questions.question:
Select the letter-cluster that is related to the third cluster in the same way as the second is related to the first.
ACE : FHJ :: MOQ : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward: A→F, C→H, E→J. So M→R, O→T, Q→V.

questions.question: Select the letter-pair that does not belong to the group.
questions.explanation: In BD, FH and JL there is a gap of one letter (+2). In NQ the gap is two letters (+3).

questions.question:
Select the number that will come next in the series.
6, 11, 21, 36, 56, ?
questions.explanation: Differences: 5, 10, 15, 20, so next is 25: 56 + 25 = 81.

questions.question:
Select the number that will come next in the series.
0, 6, 24, 60, 120, ?
If MONDAY is written as NPOEBZ in a certain code, how will FRIDAY be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: F→G, R→S, I→J, D→E, A→B, Y→Z.

questions.question: If PEN = 35 in a certain code, what is INK equal to in the same code?
'A + B' means A is the mother of B; 'A − B' means A is the brother of B; 'A × B' means A is the father of B. What does 'P × Q − R' mean?
options: P is the uncle of R
P is the brother of R
P is the father of R
P is the grandfather of R
questions.explanation: P × Q: P is the father of Q. Q − R: Q is the brother of R, so R is also P's child. Hence P is the father of R.

questions.question: A man walks 30 m towards South, turns left and walks 40 m, then turns left again and walks 30 m. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: South 30 → (0, −30); left of South is East: 40 → (40, −30); left of East is North: 30 → (40, 0). He is 40 m East of the start.

questions.question:
Statements:
All teachers are graduates.
Some graduates are engineers.
Conclusions:
I. Some teachers are engineers.
II. All engineers are graduates.
Which conclusion(s) follow(s)?
questions.explanation: The engineers who are graduates need not be teachers, so I is not certain. 'Some graduates are engineers' does not make all engineers graduates, so II does not follow.

questions.question:
If '÷' means '+', '×' means '−', '+' means '×' and '−' means '÷', what is the value of:
12 + 3 ÷ 40 − 8 × 6
If 2 * 3 = 13 and 3 * 4 = 25, then what is 4 * 5?
In a class of 45 students, Priya ranks 18th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?

Arrange the following words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary.
1. Gather  2. Garden  3. Gallop  4. Gamble  5. Gaze
questions.explanation: Compare the third letters: Ga-l, Ga-m, Ga-r, Ga-t, Ga-z → Gallop, Gamble, Garden, Gather, Gaze = 3, 4, 2, 1, 5.

questions.question: 26 January 1950, the day the Constitution of India came into force, fell on which day of the week?
questions.explanation: Odd-day method: 1600 years → 0 odd days; 300 years → 1; 49 years (12 leap + 37 ordinary) → 12×2 + 37 = 61 → 5 odd days; 26 days of January → 5. Total = 11 → 4 odd days = Thursday.

questions.question: Who was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session of 1917. Sarojini Naidu (Kanpur, 1925) was the first Indian woman President.

questions.question: Who among the following is regarded as the founder of the Ghadar Party (1913)?
questions.explanation: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 on the Pacific coast of the USA by Lala Har Dayal along with Sohan Singh Bhakna and others.

questions.question: The Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal (1793) was introduced by which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement (Zamindari system) in 1793.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the office of the Attorney General of India?
questions.explanation: Article 76 – Attorney General; 148 – CAG; 165 – Advocate General of a State; 124 – Supreme Court.

questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.explanation: The CEC and other Election Commissioners are appointed by the President (Article 324).

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX (Panchayats) and the Eleventh Schedule; the 74th did the same for municipalities.

questions.question: Which mountain pass connects Srinagar with Leh?
questions.explanation: Zoji La lies on the Srinagar–Leh highway. Nathu La is in Sikkim, Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh, Bomdi La in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.explanation: Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir is the largest freshwater lake; Chilika is a brackish-water lagoon.

questions.question: The Sundarbans delta is formed mainly by which rivers?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans lie in the Ganga–Brahmaputra (–Meghna) delta shared by India and Bangladesh.

questions.question: The financial year of the Government of India runs from:
questions.explanation: India's fiscal year begins on 1 April and ends on 31 March.

questions.question: In which of the following does sound travel the fastest?
questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids (about 5,000+ m/s in steel), slower in water and slowest in air; it cannot travel in a vacuum.

questions.question: Which acid is mainly present in lemon?
questions.explanation: Lemons and other citrus fruits contain citric acid; vinegar has acetic acid and curd lactic acid.

questions.question: Malaria is caused by:
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the protozoan parasite Plasmodium, transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito.

questions.question: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) was originally raised in 1939 under which name?
questions.explanation: CRPF was raised on 27 July 1939 as the Crown Representative's Police and renamed CRPF by an Act of Parliament in 1949.

questions.question: The Param Vir Chakra is awarded for:
options: The highest degree of gallantry in the presence of the enemy
questions.explanation: The Param Vir Chakra is India's highest wartime gallantry award; the Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry award.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2³¹ is divided by 5?
questions.explanation: Powers of 2 mod 5 cycle as 2, 4, 3, 1. 31 = 4 × 7 + 3, so the remainder is the 3rd term = 3.

questions.question: How many factors does 72 have?
questions.explanation: 72 = 2³ × 3². Number of factors = (3 + 1)(2 + 1) = 12.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the winner got 58% of the valid votes and won by 2,880 votes. What was the total number of valid votes?
questions.explanation: Margin = 58% − 42% = 16% of valid votes = 2880 → total = 18,000.

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper claims to sell rice at cost price but uses a weight of 900 g instead of 1 kg. What is his gain percentage?
questions.explanation: Gain % = (error/true weight given) × 100 = 100/900 × 100 = 11 1/9 %.

questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹8,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum, compounded annually?
A and B invest ₹24,000 and ₹36,000 respectively in a business for the same period. Out of a profit of ₹15,000, what is B's share?
A 60-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 1 : 2?
questions.explanation: Milk = 40 L, water = 20 L. For 1 : 2, water must be 80 L, so add 60 L.

questions.question: A and B together can do a work in 8 days; A alone can do it in 12 days. In how many days can B alone do it?
questions.explanation: B's one-day work = 1/8 − 1/12 = 1/24, so 24 days.

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 100 m are running in opposite directions at 50 km/h and 40 km/h. In how much time will they cross each other?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Time = (150 + 100)/25 = 10 s.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How long will the boat take to travel 36 km downstream?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 18 km/h; time = 36/18 = 2 h.

questions.question: If x = √3 + √2, what is the value of x + 1/x?
In a right-angled triangle, the two sides containing the right angle are 9 cm and 12 cm. What is the length of the median drawn to the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse = √(81 + 144) = 15 cm. The median to the hypotenuse is half of it = 7.5 cm.

questions.question: What is the total surface area of a closed cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
If tan θ = 3/4 and θ is acute, what is the value of (sin θ + cos θ)/(sin θ − cos θ)?
Number of candidates who qualified from a centre: 2022 – 450, 2023 – 540, 2024 – 486, 2025 – 630. What is the percentage increase from 2022 to 2025?

Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
METICULOUS
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail – painstaking.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
VALIANT
questions.explanation: Valiant means brave, courageous.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
BENEVOLENT
questions.explanation: Benevolent (well-meaning, kind) is opposite to malevolent (wishing harm).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom.
To bite the bullet
options: To be injured in a fight
To face a difficult situation with courage
questions.explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to make oneself do something unpleasant or difficult bravely.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom.
To be on the horns of a dilemma
options: To be in a very aggressive mood
To face a choice between two equally unpleasant options
questions.explanation: Being on the horns of a dilemma means having to choose between two equally undesirable alternatives.

questions.question:
Select the one-word substitute for the given phrase.
The killing of one's own brother
questions.explanation: Fratricide = killing a brother; patricide = father; regicide = king; genocide = a whole people.

questions.question:
Select the one-word substitute for the given phrase.
Government by the people, usually through elected representatives
questions.explanation: Democracy is government by the people. Autocracy = rule by one person with absolute power; oligarchy = rule by a few.

questions.question: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'lieutenant'.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error, or 'No error'.
The police / has arrested / the culprit.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is a plural noun, so it takes a plural verb: The police have arrested the culprit.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error, or 'No error'.
No sooner did / the bell ring / when the students rushed out.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than', not 'when': No sooner did the bell ring than the students rushed out.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bracketed part of the sentence.
He [insisted to go] there alone.
questions.explanation: 'Insist' takes the preposition 'on' followed by a gerund: insisted on going.

questions.question:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.
They will complete the project by Friday.
options: The project would be completed by them by Friday.
The project will have been completed by them by Friday.
The project is completed by them by Friday.
The project will be completed by them by Friday.
questions.explanation: Simple future active (will complete) becomes 'will be completed' in the passive.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
The officer said to the constable, "Close the gate at once."
options: The officer said to the constable that close the gate at once.
The officer ordered the constable that he closes the gate at once.
The officer ordered the constable to close the gate at once.
The officer ordered the constable to have closed the gate at once.
questions.explanation: An imperative (command) is reported with 'ordered + object + to-infinitive': ordered the constable to close the gate at once.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option for the numbered blank.

Community policing is based on the idea that the police and the public are partners. When officers walk the same streets every day, residents begin to (1) ______ them and share information more freely. This trust, in turn, helps the police to (2) ______ crimes before they happen.

Select the most appropriate option for blank (1).
questions.explanation: The next sentence refers to 'This trust', so residents begin to trust the officers.

questions.question:
Read the passage and select the most appropriate option for the numbered blank.

Community policing is based on the idea that the police and the public are partners. When officers walk the same streets every day, residents begin to (1) ______ them and share information more freely. This trust, in turn, helps the police to (2) ______ crimes before they happen.

Select the most appropriate option for blank (2).
questions.explanation: Acting 'before they happen' means the police can prevent crimes.
